title: Breadth-first search
description:
Graphs here are adjacency lists: `adj[u]` lists the neighbours of vertex `u` (for undirected graphs, each edge appears in both lists).

```cpp
using Graph = std::vector<std::vector<int>>;

std::vector<int> distances(const Graph& adj, int source);              // -1 for unreachable vertices
std::vector<int> shortestPath(const Graph& adj, int from, int to);     // the vertices on a shortest path, or {} if none
int components(const Graph& adj);                                      // for an undirected graph
bool isBipartite(const Graph& adj);
int nearestExitSteps(const std::vector<std::string>& grid);            // multi-source BFS on a grid
```

- `shortestPath`: when several shortest paths exist, return the one BFS finds when it scans each adjacency list **in order** and records the first parent of each vertex. `shortestPath(adj, v, v)` is `{ v }`.
- `nearestExitSteps`: the grid has walls `#`, open cells `.`, people `P` (open cells) and exits `E`. Return the **largest** number of steps any person needs to reach their nearest exit (moving up, down, left, right through non-wall cells), or `-1` if some person cannot reach any exit. With no people, return 0. Start the BFS from **all exits at once**: one pass, O(rows × cols).
hints: For the shortest path, store `parent[v] = u` when BFS first reaches `v`, then walk the parents back from `to` and reverse.
Multi-source BFS: push **every** exit into the queue with distance 0 before the loop starts. The first time BFS reaches a cell, it is from the nearest exit.
